# Six problems, one diagnosis discipline

This section is intentionally not a second lesson. The tools were developed in
Sections 64 and 65; the contest tests whether you can recognize them after the
surface vocabulary changes.

Before coding a problem, write:

```text
exact requested family:
easier cumulative family or coefficient model:
inversion / coefficient extraction step:
target complexity from constraints:
independent tiny oracle:
```

# Contest set

| Problem | Title |
|---|---|
| A | Primitive Necklaces |
| B | Totient Interval |
| C | Wildcard Rotation |
| D | Weighted Compositions |
| E | Black-Box Walks |
| F | GCD-One Size Spectrum |

# Escalation pattern

A and B test whether the arithmetic identities survived without the lesson's
labels. C asks you to derive an index correlation with wildcards. D requires a
sparse generating polynomial for each bounded choice. E converts a graph into
a scalar sequence before applying algebra. F changes the requested output from
one subset count to all subset sizes, forcing a second transform after Mobius
inclusion-exclusion.

# Proof checkpoints

- A: why does “minimal period exactly `n`” invert periods dividing `n`, and why
  does dividing by `n` count rotation classes?
- B: why is subtraction of two summatory values valid modulo the prime?
- C: which exact coefficient represents shift `r`?
- D: why can degrees above `K` be discarded permanently?
- E: why must the scalar walk-count sequence satisfy a recurrence of order at
  most the number of vertices?
- F: why does the Mobius-weighted sum count gcd exactly one for each fixed
  subset size, and how is the remaining binomial sum one convolution?

# Exercises

Solve all six as a timed set. During the upsolve, produce a brute generator for
each problem before reading the optimized code. The editorial's random tests
use independent definitions and are suitable models.

# Submission checklist

- I derived every reversal/offset instead of copying it from memory.
- All modular subtractions are normalized.
- The NTT is padded to the full linear-convolution length.
- Large integer products and quotient-block endpoints are safe.
- I tested degenerate algebra: order-zero recurrence, all wildcards, `n=1`,
  and target sum zero.
